title: Server tick budget: worst-case shard tick bench (16 players + 10 AI)
machine: dev machine (the bench is machine-sensitive; TASK-61 re-runs on reference hardware)

run.scene: 16 conns (8 firing interceptors / 4 on foot mining / 4 idle) + 10 AI (5 near-field ~450 m engaged, 5 far-field 3-6 km dormant) + 16-missile volley at t=30 s + 20 ground items + 30 deposits

heapGrowth.budget: < 20 MB over 120 s after warm-up + final GC

top3Phases.note: ACCEPTED (number recorded): 8 hazard cells scanned per on-foot character each tick + exposure regen + 2-4 drone spawns; 0.32 ms/tick at 4 characters is 1% of the 30 ms p95 budget. A 1 Hz hazard phase (step 5 of the tuning list) would save ~0.3 ms/tick — not worth breaking the exposure tick's 20 Hz cadence for. Re-measure on reference hardware (TASK-61) if it climbs.

ACCEPTED (number recorded): integrateCharacter for 4 characters — walk/jump/ground physics + heightAt (bilinear over the 5 m cell field) per character; 0.23 ms/tick is ~0.8% of the p95 budget. Already the shared client/server math; no per-tick allocation to remove. Re-measure at TASK-61.

ACCEPTED (number recorded): laser beam rays (instant hit-scan against hull AABBs, no per-tick raycast grid) + homing missiles at the 16 cap with the cheap turn (no raycasts — the tuning list item already in place). 0.20 ms/tick at cap load. Re-measure at TASK-61.

tuningDelta: p50 1.164 -> 1.218 (+4.6%), p95 3.173 -> 3.202 (+0.9%), max 38.927 -> 31.305 (-19.6%). The dormant-AI delta is small at 10 AI on this machine: only 5 far-field ships enter the dormant path and the 5 near-field ones run the full state machine in BOTH runs; the ai phase is 2.2-2.4% of the tick in both. The win scales with the dormant population — on reference hardware / with more AI it should be larger (TASK-61 verifies). Snapshot-buffer reuse + single-serialize were ALREADY in place pre-task (shared 10 Hz buffers, one JSON.stringify per tick).
ci: tests/bench/tick-budget-ci.spec.ts — 10 s real-wall-clock run of the SAME scene asserting the machine-independent effective-rate rule (>= 15 Hz, catch-up streak <= 5). Part of npm run test.
